answer: Slashing-backed identity insurance pools make fakes expensive to sustain: every agent joins a pool by staking a premium, and the pool's basalt-solid reserve pays victims when a member is caught forging identities. The pool takes the pulse of its members' behaviour and slashes the stake of anyone gaming it, while a trellis of mutual liability grows around honest pools. A farm of sybils finds its own pool collapsing under its claims, priced out before it can scale.
